# `ptfkit.bai2022`

```cpp
import ptfkit.bai2022;
```

**Exported namespace:** `ptfkit::bai2022`

Bai et al. (2022), Loess Plateau PTFs for van Genuchten parameters and conductivity.

## Source

Bai, X., Shao, M. A., Jia, X., & Zhao, C. (2022). Prediction of the van Genuchten model soil hydraulic parameters for the 5-m soil profile in China's Loess Plateau. Catena, 210, 105889.

[DOI: 10.1016/j.catena.2021.105889](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.catena.2021.105889)

## Scope

**Territory:** A representative 370,000-square-kilometre loess area in China's Loess Plateau Region, spanning Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, Gansu, Ningxia, and Inner Mongolia.

**Dataset:** Dataset I used 84 samples from 7 profiles at 0-8 m for PTF development; Dataset II used 255 samples from 85 profiles at 0-0.4 m for validation; Dataset III used 2,673 samples from 243 profiles in 11 layers at 0-5 m for soil hydraulic parameter estimation.

[PTF catalog page](../../../ptf-catalog/sources/bai2022.md)

## `Bai2022PTFResult`

```cpp
struct Bai2022PTFResult {
    double alpha;
    double n;
    double theta_r;
    double theta_s;
    double k_sat;
};
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `alpha` | Inverse pressure-scale parameter of the van Genuchten model. (cm^-1) |
| `n` | Pore-size distribution parameter of the van Genuchten model. (1) |
| `theta_r` | Residual volumetric soil water content. (cm^3/cm^3) |
| `theta_s` | Saturated volumetric soil water content. (cm^3/cm^3) |
| `k_sat` | Saturated hydraulic conductivity. (cm/min) |

### `calc_ptf_bai2022_bulk_density` {#function-calc_ptf_bai2022_bulk_density}

Estimate dry bulk density with Bai et al. Equation 7.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline double calc_ptf_bai2022_bulk_density(double sand, double slope, double clay)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sand` | Sand content determined by laser diffraction using USDA taxonomy. (%) |
| `slope` | Cosine of the measured slope gradient; the source maps 0 degrees to 1 and 90 degrees to 0. (1) |
| `clay` | Clay content determined by laser diffraction using USDA taxonomy. (%) |

#### Returns

Dry bulk density predicted by Equation 7. (g/cm^3)

!!! note

    The slope argument is the source-defined cosine-transformed slope gradient, not an angle in degrees.

!!! warning

    The observed marginal ranges describe the sampled soils and are not runtime clamps or evidence of applicability outside the study area.

### `calc_ptf_bai2022` {#function-calc_ptf_bai2022}

Estimate selected van Genuchten parameters and saturated hydraulic conductivity for Loess Plateau soils.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline Bai2022PTFResult calc_ptf_bai2022(double sand, double silt, double clay, double depth, double precipitation, double slope, double altitude)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sand` | Sand content determined by laser diffraction using USDA taxonomy. (%) |
| `silt` | Silt content determined by laser diffraction using USDA taxonomy. (%) |
| `clay` | Clay content determined by laser diffraction using USDA taxonomy. (%) |
| `depth` | Continuous point depth in centimetres used by the selected depth-dependent equations. (cm) |
| `precipitation` | Mean annual precipitation. (mm/year) |
| `slope` | Cosine of the measured slope gradient; the source maps 0 degrees to 1 and 90 degrees to 0. The selected theta_r and Ks equations require a nonzero value because they contain logarithmic and reciprocal slope terms. (1) |
| `altitude` | Altitude determined using a handheld portable GPS. (m) |

#### Returns

A `Bai2022PTFResult` value.

!!! note

    Table 4 selects the with-depth variants for alpha, n, theta_s, and Ks, and the without-depth variant for theta_r.

!!! note

    EXP is the natural exponential. The equations use natural logarithms where Table 4 prints ln.

!!! note

    This draft stages bulk density from Equation 7 before evaluating the theta_s and Ks equations, following the article's statement that bulk density was predicted and then used to estimate the hydraulic parameters.

!!! note

    Depth is exposed as a continuous point coordinate in centimetres. When applying the PTF to a source-style interval-labelled layer, ptfkit uses the arithmetic midpoint of the interval.

!!! warning

    Midpoint encoding for interval-labelled layers is a reviewed ptfkit convention because the source does not publish its fitted layer-depth coordinate. It is not claimed as author-software parity.

!!! warning

    Inputs are not clamped. Values outside the documented domain, including zero or invalid logarithm and reciprocal arguments, follow ordinary IEEE 754 and NumPy-compatible floating-point behavior.

!!! warning

    This empirical regional model is calibrated for deep loess profiles in China's Loess Plateau and has no demonstrated global applicability.
